title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: Objection 6 — King principal/subjects; Adam alone
pass_a_gloss: Sixth: a King makes war on a neighboring people not by himself alone but through subjects. He commands, they execute; he is principal cause, they instrumental; and even those who do not mix in the war are bound as subjects to obey the King and guard and help him with their strength. But Adam sinned alone: he commanded that sin of his to himself, not to us; he alone what he commanded himself put into execution and finished in deed. None of posterity shared in that action or put mind or hand to it. Therefore he was not the principal cause of that sin with posterity as instrumental causes. We did not fit ourselves to him as members, organs, subjects, or servants to commit that sin, but he alone, as he then stood in the nature of things, committed it by himself, and none of posterity was with him. War is the common work of King and subjects done by the kingdom's body; Adam's actual sin, as the opponent himself speaks, was of one person.
pass_b_english: Sixth. A King does not wage war on his neighbors by his own hand alone: he orders, and subjects carry out; he is the principal cause, they the instrumental—and even those who never take the field remain bound, as subjects, to obey him and to shield and aid him with their strength. Adam is not like that King. He sinned by himself. He laid that command of sin on himself, not on us; he alone executed what he had commanded himself and finished it in deed. No one among his posterity joined that action, nor lent mind or hand. So the scheme of principal and instrumental causes fails here: we did not lend ourselves to him as members, organs, subjects, or servants for committing that crime. He alone, as he then stood among the things that were, committed it through himself, and none of posterity stood with him at it. War is the shared work of King and subjects and is done by the kingdom's body; Adam's actual sin—as you yourself speak—was of one person only.
source_text: Sexto, Rex bellum infert vicinae genti non per se solum, sed per subditos. Ipse imperat, subditi exequuntur. Ipse est causa principalis, subditi instrumentalis: ac illi ipsi, qui bello se non immiscent, subditi tenentur parere Regi, eumque pro viribus tueri & juvare. Adamus vero peccavit solus, ipse sibi, non nobis peccatum illud suum imperavit; ipse solus quod sibi imperavit, mandavit executioni, & opere perfecit. Posterorum nemo actioni illi interfuit, aut mentem manumve admovit suam. Non igitur ipse causa principalis fuit illius peccati, posteri causae instrumentales. Non ad committendum illud peccatum nos ei ut membra, ut organa, ut subditi, vel famuli accommodavimus, sed ipse solus, ut tunc extabat in rerum natura, ita peccatum illud per se ipsum commisit, nec posterorum quisquam illi adfuit. Bellum est commune Regis & subditorum opus, fitque a corpore regni: peccatum actuale Adami, ut tu ipse loqueris, unius personae fuit.

choices.choice: Adam not principal with us instrumental
